title: AI’s power crunch is sending data-centre builders to the banks
excerpt: With power now the binding constraint on AI, data-centre builders are seeking billions in bank financing pledges to lock in electricity and construction.
content_html:
The bottleneck in AI is no longer chips. It is power, and the scramble to secure it is sending data-centre builders to the banks for billions in financing commitments, Bloomberg reports.The shift is a big one.

For much of the AI boom the scarce resource was Nvidia’s GPUs; now it is electricity, along with the contracts, substations, and financing needed to deliver it at scale.

The numbers are staggering. The four largest cloud firms are set to spend around $725bn on AI infrastructure this year alone, and single sites now carry price tags that would once have funded a whole company, like Meta’s $13bn Texas data centre.

Power is what makes those sites so expensive. Server racks that drew about 3kW for ordinary computing now pull up to 150kW for AI, and global data-centre capacity is expected to nearly double to roughly 200GW by 2030.

That is where the banks come in. Builders want firm financing pledges before they commit to power deals and construction contracts, and the sums are large enough that no single balance sheet wants to carry them alone.

The borrowing has already reshaped credit markets. Lenders have poured into the sector, from a $5.9bn loan for one data-centre operator to a wave of bonds and private-credit deals feeding the build.

The financing is getting creative, and opaque. Oracle’s $16.3bn data-centre raise leaned on private credit after banks grew cautious, a sign of how far off the traditional path the money now travels.

Much of it sits out of plain view. Analysts estimate the sector is carrying around $1.65tn in off-balance-sheet obligations, structured through special vehicles that keep the debt off the tech giants’ own accounts.

The hunt for power is reshaping energy markets. Builders are reviving gas plants, signing nuclear deals, and jumping utility queues, turning data centres into some of the largest new electricity buyers in a generation.

The strain is landing on everyone else. Grids are creaking under the new load, and in some regions households are already paying more as data centres compete for the same electrons.

Regulators are watching uneasily. The Bank for International Settlements has flagged ‘circular financing’ between cloud firms, their suppliers, and construction lessors as one of the bigger risks to financial stability.

The building itself is a chokepoint. Fewer than ten firms in the world can deliver a hyperscale project, and one of them, Turner, is sitting on a record backlog of about $44bn with a large share tied to data centres.

Banks are not lending blindly, either. As the sums swell and the structures grow more circular, some lenders have pulled back, which is part of why builders are chasing firm pledges rather than assuming the money will be there.

Power is being locked up years ahead. Builders are signing long deals for electricity, gas, and even nuclear output, and the bank pledges are what make those commitments credible.

Underneath it all is a bet that demand shows up. The spending only pays off if AI usage keeps climbing fast enough to fill the capacity, which is why every quarter of AI revenue is now watched so closely.

There is a self-reinforcing quality to it, too. The more money commits to the build, the more the industry needs AI to keep growing to justify it, which is precisely what makes the circularity regulators fear so hard to unwind.

The scale is historic. Goldman Sachs sees cumulative spending on this buildout running into the trillions by 2030, a figure that dwarfs past infrastructure booms and leaves little room for error.

For now, the money keeps flowing toward the wall socket. The race for compute has become a race for power, and the winners may be decided less by who has the best models than by who can finance the electricity to run them.

content_html_zh:
人工智能的瓶颈不再是芯片。 据彭博社报道，它就是权力，而为了确保这种权力的争夺，数据中心建设者正在向银行寻求数十亿美元的融资承诺。这是一个重大转变。

在人工智能热潮的大部分时间里，稀缺资源是 Nvidia 的 GPU；现在是电力，以及大规模交付电力所需的合同、变电站和融资。

数字是惊人的。 仅今年，四大云公司就将在人工智能基础设施上花费约 7250 亿美元，而单个站点现在的价格标签曾经足以资助整个公司，例如 Meta 价值 130 亿美元的德克萨斯数据中心。

电力是这些网站如此昂贵的原因。 用于普通计算的服务器机架现在可用于人工智能的功率为 150kW，预计到 2030 年，全球数据中心容量将增加近一倍，达到约 200GW。

这就是银行发挥作用的地方。 建筑商在承诺电力交易和建筑合同之前希望获得坚定的融资承诺，而且资金数额足够大，没有一个资产负债表愿意单独承担这些资金。

借贷已经重塑了信贷市场。 贷款机构纷纷涌入该行业，从向一家数据中心运营商提供 59 亿美元的贷款，到推动这一建设的一波债券和私人信贷交易。

融资变得越来越有创意，而且不透明。 在银行变得谨慎之后，甲骨文为数据中心筹集的 163 亿美元资金主要依靠私人信贷，这表明资金目前的流向与传统路径相去甚远。

其中大部分都位于视线之外。 分析师估计，该行业背负着约 1.65 万亿美元的表外债务，这些债务是通过特殊工具构建的，这些工具将债务排除在科技巨头自己的账户之外。

对电力的追求正在重塑能源市场。 建筑商正在复兴天然气工厂，签署核协议，并跳过公用事业队列，将数据中心变成一代人中最大的新电力买家。

压力正在降临到其他人身上。 电网在新的负载下不堪重负，在一些地区，由于数据中心争夺相同的电力，家庭已经支付了更多费用。

监管机构正在不安地注视着。 国际清算银行将云公司、其供应商和建筑出租人之间的“循环融资”标记为金融稳定面临的更大风险之一。

建筑物本身就是一个阻塞点。 世界上只有不到 10 家公司能够交付超大规模项目，而特纳公司就是其中之一，其积压订单金额约为 440 亿美元，创历史新高，其中很大一部分与数据中心相关。

银行也不会盲目放贷。 随着资金的膨胀和结构变得更加循环，一些贷款人已经撤回，这就是为什么建筑商追逐坚定的承诺而不是假设资金会在那里的部分原因。

电力将在未来几年被锁定。 建筑商正在签署电力、天然气甚至核输出的长期协议，而银行的承诺使这些承诺变得可信。

这一切的背后都是对需求出现的赌注。 只有当人工智能的使用量持续快速增长以填满容量时，这些支出才会得到回报，这就是为什么现在每个季度的人工智能收入都受到如此密切的关注。

它也有一种自我强化的品质。 投入建设的资金越多，该行业就越需要人工智能不断发展来证明其合理性，这正是循环监管机构担心难以放松的原因。

规模是历史性的。 高盛预计，到 2030 年，这一建设的累计支出将达到数万亿美元，这一数字使过去的基础设施繁荣相形见绌，并且几乎没有犯错的空间。

目前，资金继续流向墙壁插座。 计算竞赛已经变成了电力竞赛，决定胜利者的因素可能不是谁拥有最好的模型，而是谁能提供运行这些模型的电力。
